attributes.notes:
Kvil is an eating-schedule planner for adults. No account or sign-in is required.

Tap “Let’s begin”: choose a rhythm and meal times, then preview your week and choose reminders and iCloud sync. Home follows the schedule automatically and counts down to the next opening. During an open window it shows the window without a closing countdown. “Break fast early” and “Start fast now” adjust today's opening or closing; an undo control appears after either action. Kvil does not claim that a fast was completed.

Schedule supports different weekday windows, overnight windows, changes just for today, and days off or longer breaks. Weekly edits start tomorrow. Settings is available from Schedule and History. Optional opening/closing reminders can arrive at the planned time or beforehand. They are queued about four weeks ahead and renewed when Kvil runs; Settings displays the current horizon.

Home offers “How did yesterday go?” when the previous day is eligible and unanswered. For an overnight window, that window must have closed first. Reflections describe the user's experience. Seven days of reflections and the basic weekly recap are free. History > Explore full history presents the non-consumable dev.hkarlsen06.kvil.history, which unlocks older reflections and longer recaps. Restore Purchases is available there and in Settings. Schedules, reminders, weight, Apple Health, artwork, Watch, widgets, Live Activities, and Shortcuts remain free.

Health is optional and limited to body weight. Enable weight in History or Settings. “Connect Apple Health” requests read and write authorization together. If writes are allowed, new Kvil measurements are saved to Health; “Save new weights to Health” can be turned off in Settings. If writes are denied, new measurements remain local. Health permission is not needed for scheduling. Kvil does not send Health data to a developer server.

The local SwiftData store has CloudKit mirroring disabled. Schedule sync uses the user's private CloudKit database in iCloud.dev.hkarlsen06.kvil, with the full schedule in CKRecord.encryptedValues["payload"] (Encrypted Bytes). It includes weekly times, days off, Home fasting-action timestamps, and retained schedule versions. Reflections, reflection meal times, notes, weight, and Health records are excluded. Legacy iCloud key-value data is migrated, with removal requested after the encrypted save; no new schedule payload is written there. Account changes or removal of saved cloud data pause sync. Local records are excluded from automatic backup; free JSON export/import and deletion are in Settings. Import preserves this device's sync choice. Turning sync off does not delete an existing cloud copy.

The Watch receives the current schedule through WatchConnectivity and keeps calculating when the phone is unavailable. Open Kvil on the phone after setup, then open the Watch app. The phone delivers notifications. Home and Lock Screen widgets open Kvil when tapped.

Live Activities are off by default. Turn them on in Settings, then open Kvil while fasting with the next opening within eight hours and no intervening day off. Its opening can appear on the Lock Screen and Dynamic Island on supported devices. Activities do not start from a background server. For Siri, try “When does my eating window open in Kvil” or “Open my plan in Kvil”. The same actions are in Shortcuts; Settings > Watch & widgets links there.

English and Norwegian Bokmål are included. iPhone follows system light/dark appearance; Watch uses a dark palette. Kvil has no advertising, third-party analytics, or tracking SDKs.

Landscape photography is by Kayvan Mazhar, used under the Unsplash License: https://unsplash.com/photos/a-body-of-water-surrounded-by-a-forest-UyPumfejEMI . License: https://unsplash.com/license .

Fictional history is attached in Kvil-reviewer-demo.zip. Read README.txt, turn iCloud sync off, then import reviewer-demo.json in Settings. This does not unlock purchases.
